text:
maria: FYI I saw a weird secrets collision during last night's GPU scale job. Several inference pods restarted with old DB creds and failed init. Node autoscaler spun up extra GPUs and cost spiked. Anyone else see this?
kevin: Can you paste the sealedsecret/apply logs? Also which pipeline ran and were there concurrent merges?
maria: log snippet from the deploy runner:
```
ops-deploy-runner: applying sealedsecret inference/db-creds namespace=prod commit=456def
ops-deploy-runner: applying sealedsecret inference/db-creds namespace=prod commit=123abc
sealed-secrets-controller: applied commit=123abc (timestamp=2026-03-19T03:21:14Z)
kubectl describe pod inference-xyz: initContainer failed: Invalid credentials (DB auth)
```
maria: The surprising bit is the older commit (123abc) ended up being the active secret after the two applies; looks like a race in our GitOps apply ordering when multiple CI runners push almost-simultaneous updates.
nisha: Sounds like parallel GH Actions/GitLab runners racing. We've hit this before but with different symptoms. Two mitigations: (1) add an annotation with commit timestamp/hash and an admission webhook that rejects sealing/deploying older commits; (2) use a gitops lock or serialise prod applies. Also consider adding a checksum annotation so downstream charts can detect drift.
kevin: Short-term remediation: pin the prod gitops pipeline concurrency to 1 (no parallel applies), add exponential backoff on apply failures. Medium-term: implement sync waves in Argo/Flux so sealed secrets are synced before helm charts, or use an explicit 'secrets' job that applies and waits for success before rolling inference services. In Terraform land, ensure our pipeline ordering prevents helm deploys until secrets apply finishes (depends_on in CI orchestration).
ops-bot: apply result: sealedsecrets-controller v0.17.0 - decrypt error: key mismatch for inference/db-creds commit=123abc (controller logs attached).
sre-bot: Observability: autoscaler showed a 6h window with 12 GPU nodes added, 8 removed shortly after due to crash loops. Cost estimate: ~ $1.2k spike over 6 hours. Cloud provider also returned API rate limit 429s during the provisioning burst.
maria: OK immediate plan: (A) kevin can pin CI concurrency to 1 for prod and add retry/backoff; (B) nisha can prototype admission check that rejects sealedsecrets whose commit-annotation is older than cluster's last-seen commit; (C) ops will monitor autoscaler and temporarily increase scale-down grace to avoid thrashing.
kevin: I'll open a PR now to lock the prod runner and add an annotation 'x-git-commit' on sealedsecret manifests. Will include rollout/rollback steps and a test plan in staging with parallel merges.
nisha: I'll sketch the admission webhook and a test harness; we should also add documentation to infra-runbooks for secret apply ordering.
maria: Thanks — please post PR links here and ping #incidents if autoscaler flaps again. :thumbsup:
